links.passage: Efficient irrigation is possible through the following: innovative design methods when setting up water supply systems in farms, crop productivity and water use efficiency, translation from open-channel irrigation to micro irrigation (sprinkler and drips), irrigation scheduling by using agro-climatic and edaphic data, decision support systems based on sensors, communication technologies, and advanced control systems, among others [19,20].

links.passage: Obaideen [28] further describes full automated irrigation systems as intelligent systems that enable more efficient use and sustainable management of water resources by applying only the quantities of water required by crops at the right time, determined by real-time monitoring systems.
reference_entries: Obaideen, K. An overview of smart irrigation systems using IoT. Energy Nexus 2022, 7, 100124. [CrossRef]

links.passage: Other authors have tested the systems and reported measurable improvements in water saving and water yield performance [63,66,70].
supporting_passages: As per the developments so far, smart irrigation systems typically consist of a data acquisition network of sensors, wireless communication hardware, microcontrollers and data processing units, and an irrigation actuation unit.
links.inference_note: "The systems" refers to the smart (sensor-driven, automated) irrigation systems introduced earlier in the section, whose water savings are reported.

links.passage: Although more expensive than earlier reported low-cost systems, it enabled water savings of 24% compared to unregulated uniform rate irrigation of small apple trees.
supporting_passages: In addition, Domínguez-Niño et al. [64] implemented an irrigation system using VP3 (METER Group) temperature and 10HS (METER Group) soil moisture sensors and the CR800 data logger (Campbell Scientific, Logan, UT, USA).
links.inference_note: The preceding sentence identifies the automated, water-balance scheduling system of Domínguez-Niño et al. to which the 24% saving refers.

links.passage: Barkunan et al. [63] report the highest central estimate of water savings, around 40%, with a wide confidence interval extending roughly from 20% to nearly 80%, suggesting both substantial potential and uncertainty.
supporting_passages: The forest plot presents the reported water savings (%) at a 95% confidence interval from seven studies, indicating considerable variability in water-saving potential.
links.inference_note: The forest plot synthesises water savings of the smart irrigation systems reviewed in the section, of which Barkunan et al. reports the largest.
reference_entries: Barkunan, S.R.; Bhanumathi, V.; Balakrishnan, V. Automatic irrigation system with rainfall detection in agricultural field. Measurement 2020, 156, 107552. [CrossRef]

links.passage: Results indicated that SETMI- and ISSCADA-based irrigation management reduced water use by over 50% compared to conventional soil-based scheduling, without yield penalties.
supporting_passages: Bhatti et al. [196] implemented two complementary models for determining crop water requirements and enabling variable-rate irrigation (VRI) management in corn and soybean fields in eastern Nebraska.
links.inference_note: The SETMI (PlanetScope imagery) and ISSCADA (thermal CWSI) approaches of Bhatti et al. described in preceding sentences produced the reported water-use reduction.
reference_entries: Bhatti, S.; Heeren, D.M.; O’Shaughnessy, S.A.; Neale, C.M.U.; LaRue, J.; Melvin, S.; Wilkening, E.; Bai, G. Toward automated irrigation management with integrated crop water stress index and spatial soil water balance. Precis. Agric. 2023, 24, 2223–2247. [CrossRef]

links.passage: Field experiments on soybean demonstrated >10% water savings and >13% improvement in water productivity, without yield reduction, relative to uniform-rate irrigation.
supporting_passages: Corbari et al. [201] developed a dynamic variable-rate irrigation system in Italy by coupling a crop–energy–water balance framework with satellite-based reflectance and temperature data.
links.inference_note: The satellite-driven variable-rate prescription system of Corbari et al. named earlier in the paragraph yielded the water savings.
reference_entries: Corbari, C.; Gabrieli, D.; Furlan, L.; Furlanetto, J.; Skokovic, D.; Sobrino, J.; Morari, F. Optimizing variable rate irrigation using model- and satellite-based dynamic prescription maps. Agric. Water Manag. 2024, 299, 108896. [CrossRef]

links.passage: Using humidity, temperature, and soil moisture measurements integrated within IoT platforms, fuzzy logic has been employed to control smart irrigation gates equipped with water-level and flow sensors in open-channel irrigation, achieving water savings of up to 70% [295].
reference_entries: Farooq, M.; Hussain, A.; Hashim, S.; Yang, L.; Ali, M. Automated irrigation system based on irrigation gates using fuzzy logic. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Internet of Things and Intelligent Applications (ITIA), Zadar, Croatia, 27–29 November 2020; pp. 1–5. [CrossRef]

links.passage: To enhance crop-specific precision, Kamyshova et al. [301] integrated crop and environmental data into a phytoindication ANN to generate real-time irrigation prescription maps for center-pivot systems, reducing spatial variability and increasing maize yields by 8.9%.
